audit_findings.title: FY2025 OE reflects a lower debt burden than the valuation-date capital structure
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt is $340.716 million above FY2025 average; computed sensitivity at the filed 4.2% 2026 effective rate is $14.310 million annual pretax, $10.733 million after tax at 25%, or approximately $3.98 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher interest expense reduces equity-level OE because this method retains interest expense and does not deduct debt principal in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our weighted average effective interest rate was 4.5% in 2025 and 5.2% in 2024 on average outstanding debt of $1.0 billion in 2025 versus $956.3 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: debt rose from approximately $1.0 billion average in 2025 to $1.341 billion at June 30, 2026, and six-month interest and other non-operating expense increased by $3.258 million. Even the larger computed spot-debt sensitivity would reduce base value only from $148.92 to about $144.94 and remains far below the $185.22 market price; it therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2026 year-to-date interest expense to average debt and rerun OE using a sustainable post-tax interest charge based on expected non-seasonal debt, facility rates, fees and repayments.

audit_findings.title: Temporary swap benefits may be perpetuated in terminal OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.6 million FY2025 pretax benefit; computed $7.95 million after tax at 25%, equivalent to approximately $2.95 per base-case share if removed from the entire forecast
audit_findings.mechanism: Expiration of the swaps increases interest expense and reduces projected equity-level OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The net difference between interest paid and interest received related to our swap agreements resulted in an interest benefit of $ 10.6 million in 2025, $ 12.7 million in 2024 and $ 12.2 million in 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The benefit and February 26, 2027 expiration are demonstrated, although the record does not show whether the forecast normalized them. Removing the full 2025 benefit from every projected year is conservative because the swaps remain through early 2027; even that treatment lowers base value only to about $145.97 and bull value remains below the $185.22 price. The finding therefore cannot change the current valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Model the swaps through February 2027, then rerun subsequent OE using replacement-hedge terms or the applicable variable-rate debt cost.

audit_findings.title: Working-capital reinvestment is not documented in the owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $55.371 million 2025 core working-capital use computed from receivables, inventory and accounts payable; 13.8% of the $400 million anchor and approximately $20.54 per base-case share if treated as recurring
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental receivables and inventory less supplier financing consume cash; the amount must reduce OE or be charged through the growth-reinvestment calculation exactly once.
audit_findings.evidence: Our inventory balance increased 13% to $1.5 billion at December 31, 2025 compared to $1.3 billion at December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The $400 million anchor closely matches net income plus depreciation and amortization less capital expenditures, indicating that actual working-capital cash use was not deducted directly. The filed cash-flow components show $27.324 million used for receivables, $147.405 million used for inventory and $119.358 million supplied by accounts payable. Whether the 31% RONTA mechanism separately captures normalized working-capital reinvestment is unresolved. At the demonstrated 2025 scale, omission could move base value by about $20.54 per share and materially alter intrinsic value and the buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Produce the OE workpaper and a multi-year normalization of receivables, inventory and payables, separating growth, seasonality, price-ahead purchases and acquisitions; then rerun the DCF with normalized working-capital reinvestment included exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a nonrecurring equity-award tax windfall
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.6 million after-tax, $0.12 reported diluted EPS, and approximately $1.70 per base-case valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: The tax benefit raises net income and therefore OE unless explicitly removed or normalized.
audit_findings.evidence: We recorded a $4.6 million, or $0.12 per diluted share, tax benefit from Accounting Standards Update (ASU) 2016-09, Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting, in 2025 compared to an $8.8 million, or $0.23 per diluted share, tax benefit in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The anchor's close correspondence to GAAP net income plus depreciation and amortization less capital expenditures indicates that the $4.6 million benefit was retained. This is a demonstrated normalization error, but removing it would lower base value only from $148.92 to about $147.22 and would not change the conclusion relative to the $185.22 price.
audit_findings.action: Remove the $4.6 million FY2025 benefit from anchor OE and rerun the valuation; use the company's tax rate excluding ASU 2016-09 benefits for projections.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include operating cash rather than true surplus cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum $28.762 million, or approximately $0.76 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Only surplus cash belongs in the equity bridge; required operating cash already supports the OE stream and should not be added separately.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary capital needs are seasonal working capital obligations, debt repayment obligations and other general corporate initiatives, including acquisitions, opening new sales centers, technology-related investments, dividend payments and discretionary share repurchases.
audit_findings.explanation: The operating-cash requirement is unresolved, but the entire disputed add-back is only $28.762 million. Removing all of it would reduce base value from $148.92 to about $148.16 and bull value from $166.21 to about $165.45, both still below the $185.22 market price. Thus even the maximum possible correction is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum seasonal operating cash, foreign-cash restrictions and immediately accessible balances; add only verified surplus cash, although a zero-cash-add-back rerun is sufficient for a conservative decision check.
